title: Current Affairs (Apr–Sep 2026)
summary: Month-wise current affairs for the Apr–Sep 2026 exam window — appointments, awards, sports winners, summits, schemes, defence and space — exam-relevant items only, plus the standing officeholder anchors SSC expects you to know cold.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: "Who won the 2026 …?" or "India won the … Cup by defeating —"
pyqPatterns.approach: Sports winners and award names are pure recall — one-line anchors, no logic to fall back on. Revise the tables, don't read articles.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Four award/person or place/event pairs; 'which of the following is correctly matched?'
pyqPatterns.approach: SSC builds one wrong pair by swapping a neighbouring fact (host city, year, award). Check the pair you are most sure of first and eliminate.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: "Who took charge as … in 2026?" or a current-affairs-based statement question
pyqPatterns.approach: Keep the officeholder ladder current: CDS, COAS, CJI, CEC, RBI Governor, plus 2026's new appointments. SSC rarely digs below these.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Arrange 3-4 events of the past year in order
pyqPatterns.approach: Anchor on months — event order questions in 2026 papers came almost entirely from the Jan–Sep 2026 news cycle.

subtopics.title: March 2026 — pre-window anchors you must still know
subtopics.concept:
These events fall just before the standard 6-month window but were asked repeatedly in 2026 shifts, so learn them first.

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 8 Mar 2026 | **India won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026**, defeating **New Zealand by 96 runs** in the final at **Ahmedabad** — the first team to win back-to-back T20 World Cups (2024 & 2026). Captain: **Suryakumar Yadav**. |
| 15 Mar 2026 | **98th Academy Awards** (Dolby Theatre, hosted by Conan O'Brien): Best Picture & Director — ***One Battle After Another*** (Paul Thomas Anderson); Best Actor — **Michael B. Jordan** (*Sinners*); Best Actress — **Jessie Buckley** (*Hamnet*). |
| 19 Mar 2026 | **National Dental Commission** set up, replacing the **Dental Council of India**. |
| 28 Mar 2026 | **Noida International Airport** (Jewar, Gautam Buddha Nagar, **Uttar Pradesh**) inaugurated. |
| 30 Mar 2026 | Government declared the **Naxalite insurgency ended** (Amit Shah's statement in Parliament). |
| — | **Bhubaneswar** chosen to host the **2028 World Athletics Indoor Championships**. |

tricks.title: T20 WC 2026 = 96 from 26
tricks.body: India beat **New Zealand by 96 runs** at **Ahmedabad**; pair it with 2024 (won in Barbados vs South Africa) to own the back-to-back story.

tricks.title: Oscars ladder for 2026
tricks.body: ***One Battle After Another*** swept 6 awards including the **inaugural Best Casting**; Michael B. Jordan became only the **second actor after Lee Marvin (Cat Ballou, 1965)** to win for a dual role.

mistakes: The T20 WC 2026 co-hosts were **India and Sri Lanka**, but the final was **India vs New Zealand** — Sri Lanka was not in the final.
Noida International Airport is at **Jewar (Gautam Buddha Nagar, UP)** — do not confuse it with Delhi's IGI or the Naini airport in Prayagraj.

subtopics.title: April 2026
subtopics.concept:
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| Apr 9 | **Assembly election results**: BJP retained **Assam**; **UDF won Kerala**; big swings in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. |
| Apr 14 | **Samrat Choudhary** took over as **Bihar CM** (succeeding Nitish Kumar). |
| Apr 20 | **Laureus World Sports Awards 2026** ceremony held in **Madrid, Spain**. |
| Apr 28 | **India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement** signed in New Delhi. |
| — | **Telangana** made **cancer a notifiable disease** (first among big states to mandate reporting). |

tricks.title: FTA season
tricks.body: 2026 was India's FTA year: **EU (Jan) → New Zealand (Apr)** — remember the sequence 'big bloc first, Kiwis next'.

mistakes: Laureus 2026 venue is **Madrid**; the 2025 edition was in Madrid too but do not mix it with Monaco (older editions).

subtopics.title: May 2026
subtopics.concept:
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| May 9 | **Suvendu Adhikari** sworn in as **West Bengal CM**. |
| May 10 | Actor-politician **Vijay (TVK)** became **Tamil Nadu CM**. |
| May 14 | **V. D. Satheesan** became **Kerala CM**. |
| May 28 | **D. K. Shivakumar** replaced Siddaramaiah as **Karnataka CM**. |
| May 31 | **IPL 2026 final** (Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad): **Royal Challengers Bengaluru beat Gujarat Titans by 5 wickets** — RCB's **second straight title** (2025 & 2026) and the **first franchise to win the IPL and the Women's Premier League in the same year**. Most runs & MVP: **Vaibhav Sooryavanshi** (RR, 776 runs); most wickets: **Kagiso Rabada** (GT, 29). |

tricks.title: IPL 2026 numbers
tricks.body: **RCB × GT, 5 wickets, 31 May, Ahmedabad.** Orange Cap + MVP: **Sooryavanshi 776**; Purple Cap: **Rabada 29**.

mistakes: RCB beat **Gujarat Titans** in the final — Punjab Kings were the 2025 finalists, a common swap in wrong options.

subtopics.title: June 2026
subtopics.concept:
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| Jun 15 | DRDO flight-tested the **Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile (LRLACM)** from **Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha**. |
| Jun 30 | **General Dhiraj Seth** took charge as **Chief of the Army Staff (COAS)**. |
| Jun (mid) | **Swaminathan Janakiraman** re-appointed as **RBI Deputy Governor** for another term. |

tricks.title: Army vs CDS ladder
tricks.body: **COAS (Jun 30): Dhiraj Seth** · **CDS (May 31): N. S. Raja Subramani** — two different chairs, a favourite SSC swap.

mistakes: LRLACM was tested from **Abdul Kalam Island (Wheeler Island), Odisha** — not Sriharikota, which is the launch-pad for space missions.

subtopics.title: July 2026 — the heaviest month
subtopics.concept:
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| Jul 6 | **BRICS 2026** began with India holding the **chairmanship** for the year. |
| Jul 9 | **India–Australia** defence cooperation and **uranium export** agreement signed. |
| Jul 23 – Aug 2 | **Commonwealth Games, Glasgow** (Scotland's 4th time hosting): **Australia topped the table** (70 gold, 171 total); **India finished 4th — 13 gold, 17 silver, 9 bronze (39 medals)**. |
| Jul 25 | **Sarnath (Varanasi)** designated a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**; **Pralhad Joshi** took charge as **Education Minister** (after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation). |
| Jul 30 | Parliament passed the **Anti Paper Leak Bill, 2026**. |
| Jul 31 | **Varsha Ashok Aglawe** became the **first woman Director-General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI)**. |
| Jul (early) | **Viswanathan Anand** named **interim President of FIDE**; **Anurag Jain** appointed **CEO of NITI Aayog**; RBI's revamped **Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2026** came into effect (Jul 1). |

tricks.title: Glasgow medal memory hook
tricks.body: **Australia 70 gold → India 4th with 13-17-9 (39).** India vs Scotland tie-break on golds is why India edged the host for 4th.

tricks.title: Sarnath joins the list
tricks.body: Sarnath = **Buddha's first sermon (Dhammachakra Pravartana)** site. It joined UNESCO in **July 2026**; don't confuse with Sanchi (listed 1989) or Nalanda (2016).

mistakes: BRICS 2026 has two dates: the **chairmanship began ~Jul 6** and the **18th Summit met Sep 12 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi** — questions may target either.
Uranium exports to India came from **Australia** (Jul 9 agreement) — Canada is the wrong-pair favourite.

subtopics.title: August 2026
subtopics.concept:
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| Aug 1 | PM inaugurated **Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport** at **Bhogapuram, Andhra Pradesh**. |
| Aug 1 | **Ajit Doval** received the **Lokmanya Tilak National Award** (Pune). |
| Aug 21 | IN-SPACe chairman **Pawan Goenka** announced **ISRO will stop building launch vehicles**, transferring that role to the Indian private sector. |
| Aug 26 | Government permitted transfer of **DRDO missile technologies to private companies**. |

tricks.title: Private-sector space pivot
tricks.body: Two August moves in one line: **ISRO exits launch-vehicle building (Aug 21)** and **DRDO shares missile tech with industry (Aug 26)** — the 'privatise the hard tech' month.

mistakes: **Alluri Sitarama Raju** airport is at **Bhogapuram (near Visakhapatnam), AP** — not to be confused with the Noida (UP) airport inaugurated in March.

subtopics.title: September 2026
subtopics.concept:
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| Sep 12 | **18th BRICS Summit** held at **Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi** under India's chairmanship — PM Modi with President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin among the leaders. |
| Sep 19 – Oct 4 | **Asian Games (Aichi–Nagoya, Japan)** — 3rd Japanese hosting after Tokyo 1958 and Hiroshima 1994; **43 sports, 469 medal events**; new sports include **MMA, surfing, padel, BMX freestyle, teqball**; **India fielded ~500 athletes**; opening at Paloma Mizuho Stadium with Emperor Naruhito attending. |

tricks.title: Asian Games ladder for Japan
tricks.body: **Tokyo 1958 → Hiroshima 1994 → Aichi–Nagoya 2026** — three Japanese host cities, 68 years apart at the ends.

mistakes: The Games opened **19 September** but some competitions started **10 September** — both dates may appear; the official opening is the answer to 'when did the Games begin?'.

subtopics.title: Standing anchors — officeholders & awards to memorise cold
subtopics.concept:
SSC asks current officeholders without naming a date. Learn this ladder and re-verify it the week before your shift.

| Office | Holder (as of Sep 2026) |
|---|---|
| President | Droupadi Murmu |
| Vice-President | C. P. Radhakrishnan (since Sep 2025) |
| Chief Justice of India | Surya Kant (since 24 Nov 2025) |
| Chief Election Commissioner | Gyanesh Kumar (since Feb 2025) |
| RBI Governor | Sanjay Malhotra (since Dec 2024) |
| Chief of Defence Staff | N. S. Raja Subramani (since May 2026) |
| Chief of the Army Staff | Gen. Dhiraj Seth (since Jun 2026) |
| Foreign Secretary | Vikram Misri |
| FIDE (interim) President | Viswanathan Anand (Jul 2026) |
| NITI Aayog CEO | Anurag Jain (Jul 2026) |

**Nobel Prizes 2025** (announced Oct 2025; still asked through 2026):

| Prize | Winner(s) |
|---|---|
| Physics | John M. Martinis, Michel Devoret, John Clarke |
| Chemistry | Omar M. Yaghi, Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson |

**Gaganyaan status:** first **uncrewed** flight (G1) targeted within 2026; first **crewed** mission now planned for **2028**; the parachute-qualification test series ran through mid-2026. |

tricks.title: Nobel 2025 hooks
tricks.body: Peace: **Venezuelan opposition leader** (Machado). Literature: **Hungarian** novelist (Krasznahorkai) — Hungary's first Literature Nobel. Medicine: **Treg cells / peripheral tolerance** trio.

mistakes: **Dhiraj Seth is COAS; N. S. Raja Subramani is CDS** — the single most-swapped pair in 2026 mock papers.
Nobel Peace 2025 went to **María Corina Machado**; Nihon Hidankyo won it in **2024**.

solvedExamples.q: India won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026 by defeating ______ in the final.
solvedExamples.solution: The final (Ahmedabad, 8 March 2026) saw India beat **New Zealand by 96 runs**, making India the first team to defend the T20 World Cup title (2024 and 2026). Suryakumar Yadav captained the side.
solvedExamples.shortcut: T20 2026 = India + NZ + 96 runs + Ahmedabad. The 2024 final (vs South Africa, Barbados) is the classic wrong option.

solvedExamples.q: Which of the following pairs is **correctly** matched?
options: Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 — Ajit Doval
Commonwealth Games 2026 — top medal table: India
solvedExamples.solution: Ajit Doval received the **Lokmanya Tilak National Award** on 1 August 2026 (Pune). The other three are swapped: Wimbledon 2026 men's title went to **Jannik Sinner**; Nobel Peace 2025 to **María Corina Machado** (Nihon Hidankyo won 2024); the CWG 2026 table was topped by **Australia**, with India 4th.
solvedExamples.shortcut: In pair-match questions, verify the one fact you know cold (here: Australia topped Glasgow) and eliminate its wrong variant first.

solvedExamples.q:
Arrange the following events of 2026 in chronological order (earliest first):
1. 18th BRICS Summit  2. IPL 2026 final  3. Gen. Dhiraj Seth taking charge as COAS  4. Closing ceremony of the Glasgow Commonwealth Games
solvedExamples.solution: IPL final: **31 May** → COAS change: **30 June** → CWG closing: **2 August** → BRICS Summit: **12 September**. Order = **2, 3, 4, 1**.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Anchor months first (May, Jun, Aug, Sep) — the sequence falls out before you even check the option order.

practice.q: Which team won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026?
practice.solution: India defeated New Zealand by 96 runs in the final at Ahmedabad (8 March 2026) — the first back-to-back T20 World Cup titles.
practice.shortcut: 2024 + 2026 both went to India; co-host advantage in 2026.

practice.q: In the T20 World Cup 2026 final, India's opponent was —
practice.solution: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad. Sri Lanka co-hosted the event but was not in the final.
practice.shortcut: Hosts ≠ finalists — Sri Lanka is the trap option.

practice.q: Which franchise won the IPL 2026 title?
practice.solution: RCB beat Gujarat Titans by 5 wickets in the final (31 May 2026, Ahmedabad), defending their 2025 title — the first franchise to win the IPL and WPL in the same year.
practice.shortcut: RCB = back-to-back 2025 & 2026; GT was the beaten finalist.

practice.q: In the IPL 2026 final, Royal Challengers Bengaluru defeated —
practice.solution: RCB chased down Gujarat Titans to win by 5 wickets at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad. Punjab Kings were RCB's final opponents in 2025 — the classic wrong option.
practice.shortcut: 2025 final: RCB beat PBKS; 2026 final: RCB beat GT.

practice.q: Who was named the Most Valuable Player of IPL 2026?
practice.solution: Rajasthan Royals' 14-year-old sensation **Vaibhav Sooryavanshi** topped the run charts with 776 runs and was named MVP. Kagiso Rabada (29 wickets) took the Purple Cap.
practice.shortcut: Orange Cap + MVP went to the same player: Sooryavanshi, 776 runs.

practice.q: The Commonwealth Games 2026 were hosted by —
practice.solution: Glasgow, Scotland (23 July – 2 August 2026) — Scotland's fourth time hosting after Edinburgh 1970 & 1986 and Glasgow 2014. Birmingham hosted 2022.
practice.shortcut: Glasgow repeat: 2014 → 2026, stepping in as revised host.

practice.q: India finished at which position in the Commonwealth Games 2026 medal tally?
practice.solution: India stood 4th with 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze (39 medals), edging host Scotland (also 13 gold, 39 total) on the countback, behind Australia, and the top-2 medal nations.
practice.shortcut: Glasgow 2026: India 4th, 13-17-9 = 39.

practice.q: Which country topped the medal table at the Commonwealth Games 2026?
practice.solution: Australia topped the table for the third consecutive Games with 70 gold and 171 total medals.
practice.shortcut: Australia has topped every CWG medal table since 2006 except Birmingham 2022's tie context — default answer.

practice.q: The 18th BRICS Summit (2026) was held at —
practice.solution: India chaired BRICS in 2026 and hosted the 18th Summit on 12 September at **Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi**, with PM Modi, President Xi Jinping and President Putin among the leaders. Rio de Janeiro hosted 2025; Kazan 2024.
practice.shortcut: BRICS ladder: Kazan 2024 → Rio 2025 → New Delhi 2026.

practice.q: Who took charge as the Chief of the Army Staff on 30 June 2026?
practice.solution: General **Dhiraj Seth** became COAS on 30 June 2026. N. S. Raja Subramani had taken over as **CDS** a month earlier (31 May 2026) — a different post.
practice.shortcut: Seth = Army Chief (Jun); Subramani = CDS (May).

practice.q: Who was appointed Chief of Defence Staff in May 2026?
practice.solution: General N. S. Raja Subramani took charge as CDS on 31 May 2026, succeeding Anil Chauhan (CDS since 2022).
practice.shortcut: CDS chair changed May 2026: Chauhan → Subramani.

practice.q: Who became the first woman Director-General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI)?
practice.solution: **Varsha Ashok Aglawe** took over as the first woman DG of GSI on 31 July 2026.
practice.shortcut: First-woman 2026: Aglawe → GSI (Jul 31).

practice.q: Sarnath was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in —
practice.solution: Sarnath — where the Buddha preached his first sermon — was designated a World Heritage Site on 25 July 2026.
practice.shortcut: Sarnath = first-sermon site, listed July 2026.

practice.q: The men's singles title at Wimbledon 2026 was won by —
practice.solution: Top seed **Jannik Sinner** of Italy beat second seed Alexander Zverev in the final. Zverev is the runner-up option, not the champion.
practice.shortcut: Wimbledon 2026: Sinner over Zverev — an all top-2-seed final.

practice.q: Who won the women's singles title at Wimbledon 2026?
practice.solution: Czech ninth seed **Linda Nosková** beat fellow Czech Karolína Muchová in an all-Czech final.
practice.shortcut: All-Czech final 2026: Nosková beat Muchová.

practice.q: Which film won Best Picture at the 98th Academy Awards (2026)?
practice.solution: ***One Battle After Another*** (Paul Thomas Anderson) won Best Picture; Anderson also won Best Director, with the film taking six awards overall.
practice.shortcut: Oscars 2026 sweep: One Battle After Another = 6 awards.

practice.q: The 2026 Asian Games are being held in —
practice.solution: The XX Asian Games (19 September – 4 October 2026) are hosted by Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya — Japan's third time after Tokyo 1958 and Hiroshima 1994.
practice.shortcut: Japan ladder: Tokyo 1958 → Hiroshima 1994 → Aichi–Nagoya 2026.

practice.q: Noida International Airport, inaugurated in March 2026, is located in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
practice.solution: The airport at **Jewar** falls in **Gautam Buddha Nagar (Noida) district**, UP; the PM inaugurated it on 28 March 2026.
practice.shortcut: Noida airport = Jewar = Gautam Buddha Nagar.

practice.q: DRDO test-fired the Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile (LRLACM) in June 2026 from —
options: Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha
practice.solution: The LRLACM was flight-tested on 15 June 2026 from **Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Island (Wheeler Island), off the Odisha coast** — DRDO's dedicated missile-test island.
practice.shortcut: Missile tests → Abdul Kalam Island; space launches → Sriharikota.

practice.q: The Nobel Peace Prize 2025 was awarded to —
practice.solution: Venezuelan opposition leader **María Corina Machado** won the 2025 Peace Prize. **Nihon Hidankyo** (Japanese hibakusha group) won it in **2024**.
practice.shortcut: Peace 2025 = Machado (Venezuela); Hidankyo = 2024.

practice.q: Who took over as Chief Minister of Bihar in April 2026?
practice.solution: **Samrat Choudhary** succeeded Nitish Kumar as Bihar CM on 14 April 2026.
practice.shortcut: Bihar change 2026: Nitish → Samrat Choudhary (Apr 14).

practice.q: Who received the Lokmanya Tilak National Award in August 2026?
practice.solution: National Security Advisor **Ajit Doval** received the Lokmanya Tilak National Award on 1 August 2026 (Pune).
practice.shortcut: Tilak Award 2026 = Ajit Doval, NSA.
